65246-master-race.title: Master Race
65246-master-race.creator: Unknown
65246-master-race.description: A public-domain book from Project Gutenberg. Crouching on the floor, both arms about Rags, Eddie whispered words of reassurance while he stared up at the strange sparklings. The oak tree--the one with his tree house--was a scant quarter mile from where he knelt, and he wondered if its being so high on the ridge had caused it to draw some sort of lightning to itself. He'd read of that happening ... Or was it called Fox Fire? Eddie couldn't remember. Anyway, it looked something like that, he imagined.

arxiv-2009-13829.title: TinyGAN: Distilling BigGAN for Conditional Image Generation
arxiv-2009-13829.creator: Ting-Yun Chang, Chi-Jen Lu
arxiv-2009-13829.description: Abstract Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) have become a powerful approach for generative image modeling. However, GANs are notorious for their training instability, especially on large-scale, complex datasets. While the recent work of BigGAN has significantly improved the quality of image generation on ImageNet, it requires a huge model, making it hard to deploy on resource-constrained devices.

arxiv-2012-11720.title: KINEMATIC AZIMUTHAL ASYMMETRIES AND LAM-TUNG RELATION
arxiv-2012-11720.creator: O.V. Teryaev
arxiv-2012-11720.description: Abstract The origin of Lam-Tung relation for the angular asymmetry of Drell-Yan dileptons is analyzed. The asymmetry constrained by this relation is shown to belong to the class of kinematic azimuthal asymmetries, emerging due to the deviation of the reference axis from the natural physical one.

arxiv-2107-12986.title: 2-Way 1-Clock ATA & Its Logics: Back To The Future With Alternations This work is partially supported by the European Research Council through the SENTIENT project (ERC-2017-STG #755953).
arxiv-2107-12986.creator: Shankara Narayanan Krishna, Khushraj Madnani, Manuel Mazo Jr, Paritosh K. Pandya
arxiv-2107-12986.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Shankara Narayanan Krishna, Khushraj Madnani, Manuel Mazo Jr, Paritosh K. Pandya. In this paper, we study the extension of 1-clock Alternating Timed Automata (1-ATA) with the ability to scan the timed behaviour in both forward and backward directions: the 2-Way 1-clock Alternating Timed Automata (2-Way 1-ATA). We show that the subclass of 2-Way 1-ATA with reset free loops (2-Way 1-ATA-rfl) is expressively equivalent to MSO[ < < ] extended with Guarded Metric Quantifiers (GQMSO).

arxiv-2206-08576.title: Rules Ensemble Method with Group Lasso for Heterogeneous Treatment Effect Estimation
arxiv-2206-08576.creator: Ke Wan, Kensuke Tanioka, Toshio Shimokawa
arxiv-2206-08576.description: Abstract The increasing scientific attention given to precision medicine based on real-world data has led many recent studies to clarify the relationships between treatment effects and patient characteristics. However, this is challenging because of ubiquitous heterogeneity in the treatment effect for individuals and the real-world data on their backgrounds being complex and noisy.

arxiv-2303-12522.title: Global-in-time regular unique solutions with positive temperature to the 1d thermoelasticity
arxiv-2303-12522.creator: Piotr Michał Bies, Tomasz Cieślak
arxiv-2303-12522.description: Abstract We construct a unique regular solution to the minimal nonlinear system of the 1d thermoelasticity. The obtained solution has a positive temperature. Our approach is based on an estimate, using the Fisher information, which seems completely new in this context.

arxiv-2312-08750.title: Tomographic entanglement indicators in a coupled oscillator model
arxiv-2312-08750.creator: Sreelekshmi Pillai, S. Ramanan, V. Balakrishnan, S. Lakshmibala
arxiv-2312-08750.description: Abstract We study entanglement in a simple model comprising two coupled linear harmonic oscillators of the same natural frequency. The system is separable in the center of mass (COM) and relative coordinates into two oscillators of frequency ω c \omega_{c} and ω r \omega_{r} .

arxiv-2404-03748.title: Finite cut-off JT and Liouville quantum gravities
arxiv-2404-03748.creator: on the disk at one loop
arxiv-2404-03748.description: Abstract Within the path integral formalism, we compute the disk partition functions of two dimensional Liouville and JT quantum gravity theories coupled to a matter CFT of central charge c , with cosmological constant \Lambda , in the limit c\rightarrow-\infty , |\Lambda|\rightarrow\infty , for fixed \Lambda/c and fixed and finite disk boundary length \ell , to leading and first subleading

arxiv-2406-13606.title: DDLNet: Boosting Remote Sensing Change Detection with Dual-Domain Learning Thanks: This work was supported by the Public Welfare Science and Technology Plan of Ningbo City (2022S125), the Key Research and Development Plan of Zhejiang Province (2021C01031) and the Science and Technology Innovation 20
arxiv-2406-13606.creator: 1 st Xiaowen Ma †, 2 nd Jiawei Yang †, 3 rd Rui Che, 4 th Huanting Zhang, 5 th Wei Zhang ∗
arxiv-2406-13606.description: Abstract Remote sensing change detection (RSCD) aims to identify the changes of interest in a region by analyzing multi-temporal remote sensing images, and has an outstanding value for local development monitoring. Existing RSCD methods are devoted to contextual modeling in the spatial domain to enhance the changes of interest.

arxiv-2501-14568.title: Hybrid Quantum-Classical Multi-Agent Pathfinding
arxiv-2501-14568.creator: Thore Gerlach, Loong Kuan Lee, Frederic Barbaresco, Nico Piatkowski
arxiv-2501-14568.description: Abstract Multi-Agent Path Finding (MAPF) focuses on determining conflict-free paths for multiple agents navigating through a shared space to reach specified goal locations. This problem becomes computationally challenging, particularly when handling large numbers of agents, as frequently encountered in practical applications like coordinating autonomous vehicles. Quantum Computing (QC) is a promising candidate in overcoming such limits.

arxiv-2502-13320.title: Making the Write Connections: Linking Writing Support Tools with Writer’s Needs Conference: CHI Conference on Human Factors in Computing Systems; April 26-May 1, 2025; Yokohama, Japan CHI Conference on Human Factors in Computing Systems (CHI ’25), April 26-May 1, 2025, Yokohama, Japan DOI: 10.1145/3
arxiv-2502-13320.creator: Zixin Zhao, Damien Masson, Young-Ho Kim, Gerald Penn, Fanny Chevalier
arxiv-2502-13320.description: Abstract . This work sheds light on whether and how creative writers’ needs are met by existing research and commercial writing support tools (WST). We conducted a need finding study to gain insight into the writers’ process during creative writing through a qualitative analysis of the response from an online questionnaire and Reddit discussions on r/Writing .

arxiv-2506-18963.title: Leptogenesis in automatic Nelson-Barr models Preprint: CALT-TH/2025-020, CERN-TH-2025-118
arxiv-2506-18963.creator: C. Murgui, S. Patrone
arxiv-2506-18963.description: Abstract In this study, we numerically show that automatic Nelson-Barr models with new chiral fermions can simultaneously solve the strong CP problem and generate the observed baryon asymmetry via high-scale leptogenesis. In these models, all CP violation arises from a single spontaneous symmetry-breaking scale, linking the origin of quark and lepton CP phases.

arxiv-2510-24172.title: Unstability of numerical method for Micromagnetics Simulations with large damping parameters
arxiv-2510-24172.creator: Changjian Xie, Cheng Wang
arxiv-2510-24172.description: Abstract . We propose and implement a third-order accurate numerical scheme for the Landau-Lifshitz-Gilbert equation, which describes magnetization dynamics in ferromagnetic materials under large damping parameters. This method offers two key advantages: (1) It solves only constant-coefficient linear systems, enabling fast solvers and thus achieving much higher numerical efficiency than existing second-order methods.

arxiv-2601-20937.title: Protection of Unconventional Superconductivity from Disorder
arxiv-2601-20937.creator: Sofie Castro Holbæk, Morten H. Christensen, Andreas Kreisel, Brian M. Andersen
arxiv-2601-20937.description: Abstract Unconventional superconductivity is a desirable state of matter due to its potential for high transition temperatures T c T_{\mathrm{c}} and associated favorable superconducting properties. However, the sign-changing nature of the order parameter of unconventional superconductors renders their condensates fragile to disorder, an inevitability in real materials.

pmc-10572022.title: Examining the Effect of ALK and EGFR Mutations on Survival Outcomes in Surgical Lung Brain Metastasis Patients
pmc-10572022.creator: Sneha Sai Mannam, David P. Bray, Chibueze D. Nwagwu, Jim Zhong, Hui-Kuo Shu, Bree Eaton, Lisa Sudmeier, Subir Goyal, Christopher Deibert, Edjah K. Nduom, Jeffrey Olson, Kimberly B. Hoang
pmc-10572022.description: Simple SummaryIn this research study, the authors investigated the impact of specific genetic mutations on the survival of lung cancer patients with brain metastases who underwent surgical resection. These mutations, known as anaplastic lymphoma kinase (ALK)-rearranged and epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR)-amplified mutations, have shown potential for targeted treatments.

pmc-10689164.title: Late outcomes of renal denervation are more favourable than early ones: facts or fancies?
pmc-10689164.creator: Alexandre Persu, Maria S Stoenoiu, Frédéric Maes, Reinhold Kreutz, Giuseppe Mancia, Sverre E Kjeldsen
pmc-10689164.description: Following second-generation randomized trials, there is evidence that renal denervation (RDN) decreases blood pressure (BP), although to a lesser extent than suggested in the initial controlled and observational studies. The recent publication of the 36-month follow-up of the Symplicity HTN-3 trial has raised expectations, suggesting increasing, late benefits of the procedure, despite initially negative results.

pmc-10769514.title: The published complete mitochondrial genome of Spotted Greenshank (Tringa guttifer) is a chimera with DNA from Red-necked Stint (Calidris ruficollis) (Aves: Charadriiformes)
pmc-10769514.creator: George Sangster, Jolanda A. Luksenburg
pmc-10769514.description: A recently published complete mitochondrial genome of Spotted Greenshank (Tringa guttifer) was the first DNA sequence of this species (GenBank accession number MK905885, RefSeq number NC_044665; Liu et al. 2019, The complete mitochondrial genome of the Spotted Greenshank Tringa guttifer (Charadriiforemes [sic]: Charadriidae), Mitochondrial DNA Part B. 4:2353–2354).

pmc-11478848.title: Orthorexia as an Eating Disorder Spectrum—A Review of the Literature
pmc-11478848.creator: Izabela Łucka, Artur Mazur, Anna Łucka, Izabela Sarzyńska, Julia Trojniak, Marta Kopańska
pmc-11478848.description: Background: The purpose of this study is to compare and analyze research studies focused on orthorexia nervosa (ON) as a spectrum of eating disorders, and to summarize potential risk factors in different age and social groups. ON is characterized by an obsession with healthy eating, which leads to a restrictive diet and health problems.

pmc-11509775.title: Efficacy and Tolerability of Erenumab and Topiramate for Prevention of Chronic Migraine: A Retrospective Cohort Study
pmc-11509775.creator: Eslam El Nebrisi, Zainaba Suaad Ahmed Ruwayya, Dalya Ibrahim Alzayori, Ranya Ibrahim Alzayori, Shyam Babu Chandran, Mohamed Elshafei, Litao Yi
pmc-11509775.description: Background and Objectives: Migraine is a chronic neurological disorder affecting approximately 14% of the global population. Beyond physical pain, migraines significantly impact individuals’ quality of life, influencing education, employment, and income levels. Topiramate, a second-generation antiepileptic medication, has demonstrated notable efficacy in reducing the occurrence of chronic migraine.

pmc-11523832.title: Barriers and facilitators to conducting randomised controlled trials within routine care of neurorehabilitation centres: a qualitative study
pmc-11523832.creator: Isabella Hotz, Nathalie Ernst, Christian Brenneis, Gudrun Diermayr, Barbara Seebacher
pmc-11523832.description: BackgroundRandomised controlled trials (RCTs) are considered the gold standard for generating clinical evidence. The focus on high internal validity in RCTs challenges the external validity and generalisability of findings, potentially hindering their application in routine care. In neurorehabilitation, limited literature addresses conducting RCTs feasibly and efficiently.

pmc-12413620.title: ﻿An illustrated key to the lace bugs (Hemiptera, Heteroptera, Tingidae) from “Oriental Galapagos” (the Ogasawara Islands, Japan), with descriptions of three new species of the endemic genus Omoplax Horváth, 1912
pmc-12413620.creator: Jun Souma
pmc-12413620.description: ﻿AbstractThe lace bugs (Hemiptera, Heteroptera, Tingidae) from the Ogasawara Islands, Japan, which are known as “Oriental Galapagos”, are taxonomically revised. The following eight species belonging to the two endemic genera, Acanthomoplax Souma & Kamitani, 2021 (Tinginae, Tingini) or Omoplax Horváth, 1912 (Tinginae, Tingini) are recognized from the islands: A. tomokunii Souma & Kamitani, 2021, O. desecta (Horváth, 1912), O. hisasueisp.

pmc-12748988.title: Automation and machine learning drive rapid optimization of isoprenol production in Pseudomonas putida
pmc-12748988.creator: David N Carruthers, Patrick C Kinnunen, Yuerong Li, Yan Chen, Jennifer W Gin, Ian S Yunus, William R Galliard, Stephen Tan, Tijana Radivojevic, Paul D Adams, Anup K Singh, Jess Sustarich, Christopher J Petzold, Aindrila Mukhopadhyay, Hector Garcia Martin, Taek Soon Lee
pmc-12748988.description: Advances in genome engineering have improved our ability to perturb microbial metabolic networks, yet bioproduction campaigns often struggle with parsing complex metabolic datasets to efficiently enhance product titers. We address this challenge by coupling laboratory automation with machine learning to systematically optimize the production of isoprenol, a sustainable aviation fuel precursor, in Pseudomonas putida.

pmc-13426078.title: Prevalence, perceived effects, and motivations for adolescent e-cigarette use: A cross-sectional study in the Paris region
pmc-13426078.creator: Mathilde Gendrot, Anne-Laurence Le Faou

pmc-13455573.title: First molecular and phylogenetic characterization of Physaloptera clausa in long-eared hedgehogs (Hemiechinus auritus) from Iran
pmc-13455573.creator: Aida Vafae Eslahi, Majid Pirestani, Moslem Karami, Sasan Khazaei, Milad Badri
pmc-13455573.description: Physalopteridae nematodes pose a threat to a broad spectrum of animals including amphibians, reptiles, birds and mammals. The current study was the first molecular and phylogenetic characterization of Physaloptera clausa parasitizing long-eared hedgehogs (Hemiechinus auritus) in Iran. A male road-killed H. auritus was collected from Shahriar City, Tehran province in May 2022 and it was subjected to necropsy.

pmc-13528853.title: Laparoscopic Retroperitoneal Repair of a Retrocaval Ureter: A Case Report and Video Demonstration
pmc-13528853.creator: Mohammed Alshehri, Ebtesam Almajed, Khadijah Eid, Nojoud Alamri
pmc-13528853.description: BackgroundRetrocaval ureter is an uncommon congenital condition caused by abnormal development of the inferior vena cava. The resulting posterior displacement of the ureter may produce compression, impaired urinary drainage, and hydronephrosis.Case PresentationA 35‐year‐old man was referred following the detection of a right‐sided Type I retrocaval ureter during evaluation of right renal colic. Laboratory investigations and physical examination were unremarkable.
